strategy:
1. Approach and rationale
Use a seeded, feasible-population differential-evolution search and rank every candidate by the evaluator’s exact finite-support correlation score. Start the population with the supplied construction when it is usable, along with projected perturbations and algorithmically generated profiles. Evolve it by differential mutation, crossover, joint box-and-mass projection, and exact-score selection. Preserve a separate best-so-far candidate and fallback throughout the run.

This is materially different from an epigraph nonlinear solve, a smoothed projected-gradient search, or pairwise coordinate line minimization: it uses neither a solver nor gradients or a smoothed surrogate, and proposes population-level difference vectors rather than optimizing individual coordinate pairs. The population and restart steps are intended to explore multiple basins and reduce dependence on one local trajectory. They are heuristics; the objective is nonconvex, and neither improvement over the supplied construction nor global optimality is guaranteed. The justified correctness facts are that every accepted vector will be feasible and every reported score will use all evaluator lags and the evaluator’s scale. No improvement or achievement of the target is to be asserted in advance.

2. Mathematical specification
For a usable parent of length n, retain its native resolution. Otherwise set n=45. Let dx=2/n and S=n/2. The feasible set is the set of length-n vectors h satisfying 0≤h_i≤1 and sum_i h_i=S. This is exactly the discretized integral constraint because dx times the sum is 1.

For each integer lag k from −(n−1) through n−1, define Q_k(h)=sum over i=max(0,k) through min(n−1,n−1+k) of h_i(1−h_(i−k)). The finite-support correlation np.correlate(h, 1−h, mode='full') has entry Q_k at index k+n−1. The exact objective is C(h)=dx times max_k Q_k(h). Include all 2n−1 lags, including both lag directions and their partial-overlap boundaries. Do not use circular correlation or an autocorrelation identity that omits boundary terms. Lower C is better.

The search does not introduce an epigraph variable or claim convexity. Products of entries make the objective generally nonconvex, so differential evolution is only a heuristic. Its mutation formulas use feasible population vectors. In real arithmetic, differences of equal-mass vectors sum to zero: for target x_i, current-to-pbest mutation is v=x_i+F(x_p−x_i)+F(x_r1−x_r2); rand/1 mutation is v=x_r0+F(x_r1−x_r2). Both have sum S before crossover. Binomial crossover may change the sum, so every trial is projected onto the feasible set before scoring.

Use the Euclidean projection Pi(v) onto the box-and-sum set: Pi(v)_i=clip(v_i−lambda,0,1), where lambda is chosen so that sum_i Pi(v)_i=S. This single joint projection enforces both constraints; clipping followed by rescaling is not an acceptable substitute. The original exact score, not a population surrogate or mutation quantity, determines all candidate rankings and the returned score.

3. Implementation procedure
1. Define run(seed=42, **kwargs) at top level, with all helpers also at top level and no closures or lambdas. Use NumPy and Python math only; a general optimizer, SciPy, CVXPY, filesystem access, and network access are unnecessary. Ignore unrecognized kwargs. Initialize a NumPy Generator from seed; if that fails, initialize it with 42. Do not redefine, serialize, reconstruct, or hard-code initial_h_values.

2. Inspect initial_h_values through globals only if present. Convert it to a local float64 copy inside a guarded conversion. A usable parent must be one-dimensional, finite, have 2 through 999 entries, and have every entry in [−1e−8,1+1e−8]. Set n to its length. Project the supplied values jointly onto the box-and-sum set and require the projection to pass the feasibility check. This projection also repairs any mass error. Keep this repaired vector as an unchanged parent fallback and as the first population member. If the input is absent, malformed, outside the stated bounds, or cannot be projected, use n=45 and the constant fallback h_i=0.5. Do not change resolution or interpolate a parent.

3. Implement a top-level project_box_sum(v,S) helper. Return failure for a malformed, nonfinite vector, an invalid S, or entries with magnitude above 1e12. For length n, bracket the threshold with lo=min(v)−1 and hi=max(v); the clipped sum is n at the low end and zero at the high end. Run 80 bisection iterations. At midpoint m, if sum(clip(v−m,0,1))>S, set lo=m; otherwise set hi=m. Set y=clip(v−(lo+hi)/2,0,1). Correct the residual S−sum(y) deterministically in increasing index order: for a positive residual add at most 1−y_i to each entry; for a negative residual subtract at most y_i. Make a second pass if needed. Return failure unless y is finite, all entries are in [0,1], and the final mass error is at most 1e−10 times max(1,n). This is the only repair mechanism for parents, starts, mutations, and immigrants.

4. Implement is_feasible(h,n) to require a one-dimensional vector of length n, finite entries, bounds within 1e−12, and mass error at most 1e−10 times max(1,n). Implement exact_score(h,n) to return a nonfinite sentinel on invalid input and otherwise compute corr=np.correlate(h,1−h,mode='full'), verify its length is 2n−1 and all values are finite, then return float(max(corr)*(2.0/n)). This direct expression is authoritative. Do not score with an approximate correlation, a restricted lag set, or a mutation formula.

5. Set population size P=24 when n≤100, P=16 when 101≤n≤300, and P=10 when n>300. Set the maximum number of search score evaluations to B=min(3000,max(P+2,floor(20,000,000/n²))). Count the fallback score, initialization scores, trial scores, and restart-immigrant scores against B. The final mandatory return validation and rescoring may use up to two additional calls. Initialize the immutable fallback and its exact score before starting the search.

6. Build a population of P feasible vectors algorithmically, with the fallback first. With a parent, include its reversal, four projected parent perturbations parent+sigma*normal_noise for sigma in [0.02,0.06,0.12,0.25], four projected independent Uniform[0,1] vectors, four projected cosine profiles, and a projected block profile, taking candidates in that order until the population is full. The cosine profiles have entries 0.5+0.35*cos(2*pi*m*i/n+0.37*m), for i=0,...,n−1 and m=1,2,3,4. Without a parent, use the constant fallback, a block profile, an alternating zero/one profile, the four cosine profiles, and projected uniform vectors. Define the block profile with the first floor(n/2) entries equal to one, the remaining entries zero, and, for odd n, the next entry equal to 0.5. If these candidates do not fill P, alternate projected Gaussian perturbations of the fallback with projected uniform vectors until it is full. Project and check every start. If a start fails, put a copy of the fallback in its slot. Score each distinct slot used in the population through exact_score; update the separate best-so-far copy only for an improvement greater than 1e−12 times max(1,abs(best_score)).

7. Run synchronous differential-evolution generations: make an immutable snapshot Xold and its scores at the start of each generation, and write accepted replacements into copies Xnew and scores_new. Use a seeded random permutation of target indices. Rank Xold by exact score and define the pbest pool as the best max(2,ceil(0.2P)) members. Initialize Fmean=0.65 and CRmean=0.85. For each target independently, sample F_i by adding 0.1 times a standard Cauchy draw to Fmean, replacing a nonfinite draw by Fmean, and clipping to [0.1,1.0]. Sample CR_i by adding 0.1 times a standard-normal draw to CRmean and clipping to [0.05,1.0]. With probability 0.75 choose current-to-pbest: choose pbest uniformly from the pool excluding the target when possible, then choose distinct r1,r2 excluding the target and pbest and form v=Xold[i]+F_i*(Xold[pbest]−Xold[i])+F_i*(Xold[r1]−Xold[r2]). Otherwise choose three distinct population indices r0,r1,r2 excluding the target and form v=Xold[r0]+F_i*(Xold[r1]−Xold[r2]). P is always large enough for these choices.

8. For each mutant, form a binomial crossover trial from the target: independently choose each coordinate from the mutant with probability CR_i, retain the target otherwise, and force one uniformly selected coordinate to come from the mutant. Project the trial using project_box_sum and reject it if projection or is_feasible fails. If the search score budget remains, evaluate it with exact_score. Update the global best copy only on a strict improvement by the tolerance specified above. Replace the target in Xnew only if the trial score is lower than that target’s snapshot score by more than 1e−12 times max(1,abs(target_score)); otherwise retain the target. Record F_i and CR_i only for successful target replacements. Never rank by F, CR, population rank alone, or a surrogate. Catch exceptions or nonfinite results per trial and continue without corrupting the population or best copy.

9. At the end of each generation, commit Xnew and scores_new, including any successful proposals processed before a budget stop. If there were successful target replacements, update Fmean to 0.9*Fmean+0.1*(sum(F_i²)/sum(F_i)) over successes and CRmean to 0.9*CRmean+0.1*mean(CR_i) over successes; clip the means to [0.1,0.95] and [0.05,0.95], respectively. Track consecutive complete generations without a global-best improvement. After eight such generations, and only if budget remains, inject max(1,P//4) immigrants. For immigrant j, use a projected Uniform[0,1] vector when j mod 3 is zero; otherwise use best_h+sigma*normal_noise, with sigma=min(0.30,0.05*1.6^restart_level). Project, check, and exact-score each immigrant under the same budget. Update best_h if warranted. For each valid immigrant, replace the worst-scoring population member other than the current best-scoring member, even if the immigrant is worse; the separate best_h remains unchanged unless the immigrant improves it. Then increase restart_level by one up to four, set Fmean=min(0.95,Fmean+0.10), set CRmean=min(0.95,CRmean+0.05), and reset the no-improvement counter. This deliberate replacement restores population diversity without risking the saved best or fallback.

10. Stop when B search score evaluations are used, when the generation limit is reached (200 generations for n≤100, 120 for 101≤n≤300, or 60 for n>300), or when no further valid operation can be completed. If the budget expires partway through a generation or injection, keep all valid improvements already recorded and terminate cleanly. Keep copies of fallback_h and best_h separate from mutable population rows at all times.

11. Before returning, project best_h once more, check feasibility, and recompute its score with exact_score. Also validate and rescore the saved fallback. Return the best of these two valid vectors by exact score, preferring the fallback on a tie. If best_h’s final projection, validation, or scoring fails, use the fallback. If the fallback also fails, construct a fresh constant 0.5 vector at n=45 and score it with the same exact formula. Return a float64 NumPy vector, its Python-float exact score, and integer n_points equal to the vector length.

4. Search choices and useful variations
Use the defaults in section 3: native parent resolution, P=24/16/10 by size, Fmean=0.65, CRmean=0.85, a 20% pbest pool, 75% current-to-pbest mutation, the stated crossover, eight-generation restart interval, and the stated evaluation and generation caps. At the supplied n=45 resolution this allocates up to 3000 search score evaluations, including initialization. The seed makes all stochastic choices reproducible. No preliminary experiment is required.

Correctness requirements are fixed: score the full finite-support correlation with scale 2/n; enforce both box bounds and mass by joint projection; use the supplied usable parent at its native length and retain it as fallback; and accept and return candidates only after exact scoring and feasibility checks. Do not claim global optimality or that the target is reached. If a coder elects a different bounded configuration, practical ranges are population sizes 16–32 for n≤100 and 8–20 above 100, pbest fractions 0.10–0.30, initial Fmean 0.5–0.8, initial CRmean 0.7–0.95, and restart intervals 6–12 generations. Keep the seeded operation, finite score budget, exact objective, and feasibility rules unchanged; the stated defaults remain the recommended complete configuration.

5. Numerical robustness and memory use
Use float64 throughout. The projection bisection has a finite iteration count and deterministic residual correction; reject any result that fails the stated bounds or mass tolerance. Check inputs, generated vectors, exact correlations, scores, and adaptive parameters for finiteness. Treat invalid proposals and exceptions as rejected candidates, not reasons to lose a valid population member, best vector, or fallback. Cauchy draws are clipped as specified, and all stored scores used for selection must be finite.

The exact correlation requires O(n²) arithmetic per candidate but only O(n) correlation output memory. The population uses O(Pn) memory; mutation, projection, and score calculation use O(n) temporary vectors. Do not build an n-by-n interaction matrix, a Hessian, or a lag-by-coordinate tensor. At n=45 the population is only 24 vectors; near n=999 the population is 10 vectors and the score budget decreases with n. The fixed budget and generation limits bound one-CPU runtime. There is no external solver or parallel work. If optimization does not improve the fallback, return the feasible fallback with its exact score.

6. Runtime safeguards and return contract
All input checks, parent repair, start construction, projections, candidate feasibility decisions, exact objective evaluations, acceptance, budget enforcement, and failure recovery must be operations in the generated program. Before scoring any vector, require the correct one-dimensional shape, finite values, bounds, and sum. Before accepting any mutation or immigrant, jointly project it, verify feasibility, and calculate max(np.correlate(h,1−h,mode='full'))*(2.0/n) over all 2n−1 entries. Keep an unchanged feasible fallback and a separate best-so-far copy; exceptions, invalid vectors, nonfinite scores, and ties must not overwrite them.

Revalidate and rescore the vector selected for output immediately before returning. The top-level run(seed=42, **kwargs) must return exactly (h_values, c5_bound, n_points), with h_values a feasible float64 NumPy array, c5_bound its exact evaluator score as a Python float, and n_points=len(h_values). The program must not state that a target bound has been achieved unless its runtime-computed returned score actually satisfies it.
